title: Transfinite scheduling of persistent requirements
statement: Let D be a nonempty category admitting colimits of all nonempty linearly ordered shapes in Type w, and let A be a type in Type w. For every object X and a∈A let S(X,a) be a proposition. Assume S persists along every morphism X→Y. Assume that whenever not all S(X,a) hold, there are Y, a morphism X→Y and an a such that S(X,a) is false and S(Y,a) holds. Then there is an object X for which every S(X,a) holds.

proof.text: Argue by contradiction that every object misses a requirement. Choose for each X a successor object, an arrow to it, and a requirement absent in X but present in the successor. This is a Mathlib SmallObject.SuccStruct. Let κ be the successor cardinal of max(aleph0,|A|), and iterate along κ.ord.ToType. This well-order has no maximum. Colimits of the whole order and of each nonempty initial segment exist by hypothesis, so Mathlib’s transfinite iteration applies.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: The selected task at b holds at succ(b) by the successor identity of the iteration. If b<c, persistence makes it hold at c, whereas the selected task at c is absent there. Hence the selections define an injection from κ.ord.ToType to A. Its cardinality is κ>|A|, a contradiction. The empty A case is included: the assumption that every object misses a requirement already fails.
